key.rejection_reason: A custom hook reimplements what declarative deny rules already provide and misses coverage the rules get for free: Read deny rules also apply to @file mentions, Grep and Glob, IDE-shared context, and recognized Bash file commands like cat, head, tail, and sed. The settings docs' own secrets example uses permissions.deny, deny rules merge from every scope, and no allow rule or hook allow decision can override them.
key.context_boundary: no context window (deny rules are evaluated by Claude Code at the tool-call boundary, not by the model); what the boundary guarantees is that matching secret file contents never cross into context, with coverage extending beyond the Read tool to Grep, Glob, @file mentions, and IDE-shared context
key.lifecycle: evaluated by the permission system before every tool call; deny rules are checked before ask and allow, and deny/ask rules in project settings apply without workspace trust
key.failure_mode: Deny rules bind the built-in tools and recognized Bash file commands only; an arbitrary subprocess such as a Python script calling open() can still read the file, which only OS-level sandboxing prevents.
key.version_caveat: none for the core behavior; a Read deny rule additionally blocking the Edit tool on the same path requires v2.1.208 or later

sheets.primary: permissions.deny rules in the repo's checked-in .claude/settings.json: Read(.env), Read(.env.*) and Read(secrets/**), plus matching Edit(...) entries for the same paths. Deny rules are evaluated first by Claude Code, before ask and allow, and a deny in project settings cannot be re-allowed by a teammate's user or local settings.
sheets.rejected_alternative: A PreToolUse hook on the file tools that inspects .tool_input.file_path and exits 2. It works and is the documented pattern for protected files, but it is a script every teammate must keep functioning, and it fails open whenever the script errors, while a deny rule is evaluated unconditionally by the harness.
sheets.enforcement_owner: The harness. Permission rules are enforced by Claude Code, not by the model, so no prompt or CLAUDE.md text can loosen them.
sheets.context_boundary: Evaluated inside the Claude Code process before the tool runs, so the file contents never reach the model's context window. A scoped rule such as Read(secrets/**) leaves the Read tool visible and returns a denial to the model, whereas a bare-name deny such as Read would strip the tool from context entirely.
sheets.lifecycle: Applies from session start for every session started in the repo and for every read attempt for the life of the session. Deny and ask rules are not gated by the workspace trust dialog (only allow rules and additionalDirectories are), so a teammate gets the restriction on their first run with no acceptance step; it stops only if the rules are deleted from the file.
sheets.failure_mode: Fails closed for Claude's built-in file tools and for file commands Claude Code recognizes in Bash such as cat, head, tail and sed, and symlink tricks are covered because a deny matches either the link path or its target. It does not reach an arbitrary subprocess: a Python or Node script the agent writes can still open .env, so pair it with OS-level sandboxing (sandbox.filesystem.denyRead) if the requirement is real containment rather than tool-level refusal.
sheets.version_caveat: A Read deny rule also blocks the Edit tool on the same path only on Claude Code v2.1.208 or later, so include explicit Edit(...) deny entries for older clients. As of v2.1.210 only Read(path) and Edit(path) rules are consulted in file permission checks: a Write(secrets/**), NotebookEdit(...) or Glob(...) path rule is accepted, never used, and produces a startup warning.

sheets.primary: Permission deny rules in the repo's checked-in .claude/settings.json, denying the read-capable tools against those paths (deny entries covering Read and Glob/Grep style access to ./.env, ./.env.*, and ./secrets/**), plus matching deny entries for the Bash surface so cat/less style reads are refused too.
sheets.rejected_alternative: A PreToolUse hook that inspects each tool call's path argument and blocks it. That is more expressive but is extra code to maintain when the permission system already evaluates deny rules first.
sheets.enforcement_owner: The harness. The permission layer evaluates deny rules before the tool executes and the model never gets the file content, so this is not a matter of the model choosing to comply.
sheets.context_boundary: Evaluation happens entirely in the harness before any tool result is produced; what crosses into the model's context is only a short refusal message naming the denied tool, never the file body.
sheets.lifecycle: Applies from session start for anyone who opens the repo, because project settings are loaded with the project. It stops applying if the file is edited away, and it does not follow the secrets anywhere else on the machine.
sheets.failure_mode: It fails closed for the built-in file tools but fails open around them: a Python or Node script the agent writes and runs reads the file directly, environment variables already exported into the shell leak the same values, and any path pattern the globs did not anticipate (.env.local, secrets nested under another directory, a symlink) slips through. Deny rules also cannot stop an MCP server or subprocess from reading the same bytes.
sheets.version_caveat: Deny rules with per-tool specifiers such as Read(...) and Bash(...) are the mechanism, and deny takes precedence over allow. I cannot verify from model knowledge which release added file-read deny specifiers as distinct from Bash-only rules, nor the exact glob semantics for leading ./ versus bare patterns, so the rules must be tested against a real read attempt before being trusted.

sheets.primary: Permission deny rules in the repository's committed .claude/settings.json: Read(./.env), Read(./.env.*), Read(./secrets/**), plus matching Edit(...) deny rules so no file-editing tool can touch the same paths. Deny and ask rules restrict rather than grant, so they apply without waiting on the workspace trust dialog.
sheets.rejected_alternative: A PreToolUse hook on Edit|Write|Read that pattern-matches the path, the shape the docs show as protect-files.sh: it reimplements path matching by hand, misses Grep, Glob and @-references, and can be turned off with disableAllHooks.
sheets.enforcement_owner: The harness. The rule set is evaluated by Claude Code before the tool call is dispatched, independently of anything the model or the prompt says.
sheets.context_boundary: Evaluation happens in the harness's settings layer, outside any context window; the file contents never enter the session, and only the denial message crosses back to the model. Because the rules are committed to the repo, they apply to every teammate's session in that checkout.
sheets.lifecycle: The rules load at session start from the checked-in project settings file and apply to every matching tool call for the whole session, in every clone of the repo; they stop applying when the file is edited or when a higher-precedence scope is not involved, since deny from any scope always wins.
sheets.failure_mode: Fails closed for the built-in file tools and for file commands Claude Code recognizes in Bash such as cat, head and sed, but it is not a filesystem boundary: any subprocess the agent launches, for example a Python script, can still open the same paths. Bare-name spelling mistakes also matter, since a rule whose tool name matches nothing only produces a startup warning.
sheets.version_caveat: A Read deny rule also covers the Edit tool on the same path only from Claude Code v2.1.208 or later, and Write and NotebookEdit are never covered by a Read rule, so an explicit Edit deny rule is required. On older builds you need both Read and Edit rules spelled out.

sheets.primary: permissions.deny rules in the repo's checked-in .claude/settings.json, for example Read(.env), Read(**/.env) and Read(secrets/**). A Read deny rule also blocks the Edit tool on the matching paths, and the file ships with the repo so every clone picks it up.
sheets.rejected_alternative: A PreToolUse hook that inspects file_path and exits 2. It loses because it is a script with runtime dependencies on every teammate's machine, whereas a deny rule is declarative data the harness evaluates before hooks and ahead of any hook or model approval.
sheets.enforcement_owner: The harness. Deny rules are evaluated by Claude Code before the tool call, independently of anything the prompt or CLAUDE.md says, and they outrank a PreToolUse hook that returns allow.
sheets.context_boundary: Evaluated inside the Claude Code process before the tool executes, so the secret file's contents never enter the context window; only a denial message crosses back to the model. Subagents spawned by the session inherit the same rules.
sheets.lifecycle: Loaded at session start from the project settings file and evaluated on every matching file-tool call for the life of every session run in that repo. It stops applying if the checked-in file is edited or deleted, or when Claude Code is launched from a directory that does not resolve those project settings.
sheets.failure_mode: Fails closed for the built-in file tools and for file commands Claude Code recognises inside Bash such as cat, head, tail and sed. It fails open against indirect reads: a Python or Node script the agent writes and runs can still open .env. Project settings also live in the repo, so anyone with commit rights can weaken them.
sheets.version_caveat: No version gate applies to Read and Edit deny rules; they work on every current version. The relevant lock is an enabling flag rather than a version: to stop a developer re-allowing those paths in their own settings, an admin must set the managed-settings-only allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly, and to cover spawned processes the sandbox must be enabled as well.

scenarios.scenario: The platform team must guarantee that the only automation scripts, on-demand instruction packages, custom agent definitions, and external tool servers that ever load are the ones IT ships centrally. Nothing a developer adds on their own machine or commits into a repo may take effect.

key.primary: strictPluginOnlyCustomization in managed settings, which locks skills, agents, hooks, and MCP servers to plugin or managed sources; paired with strictKnownMarketplaces and disableSideloadFlags to control the plugin channel itself
key.rejection_reason: allowManagedHooksOnly blocks only user, project, and non-force-enabled plugin hooks; skills, custom agents, and MCP servers from user and project sources still load. strictPluginOnlyCustomization is the managed-only key documented to lock all four customization surfaces (or a named subset such as ["skills", "hooks"]) so they can come only from plugins or managed settings.
key.context_boundary: no context window (a load-time gate the harness reads from managed settings); skills, agents, hooks, and MCP servers from user and project sources are blocked from loading at all, so nothing from those sources ever reaches any session or its context
key.lifecycle: read from managed settings at startup; blocks loading of skills, agents, hooks, and MCP servers from user and project sources for the whole session
key.failure_mode: Leaves bypass channels open unless companions are set: the --plugin-dir, --plugin-url, --agents, and --mcp-config CLI flags still work without disableSideloadFlags, and marketplace sources stay open without strictKnownMarketplaces; it also blocks developers' legitimate personal tooling, forcing everything through plugin packaging.
key.version_caveat: disableSideloadFlags requires v2.1.193 or later; no version gate is documented for strictPluginOnlyCustomization itself

sheets.primary: Managed settings deployed by MDM setting strictPluginOnlyCustomization to true, so skills, agents, hooks and MCP servers load only from plugins or managed sources, combined with strictKnownMarketplaces to pin the plugin supply to IT's marketplace and disableSideloadFlags to close the CLI escape.
sheets.rejected_alternative: Shipping everything as an internal plugin and relying on the marketplace allowlist alone. It loses because without the customization lock a developer can still drop files in ~/.claude/skills, .claude/agents, hooks in project settings or a repo .mcp.json and have them load alongside the sanctioned plugin.
sheets.enforcement_owner: The harness. Claude Code decides at configuration load time which sources are eligible, and managed settings cannot be overridden by user or project files.
sheets.context_boundary: Enforced during configuration load in the CLI process, before any session context exists. Blocked skills and agents are never advertised to the model, so their content cannot cross into the main context window or into any subagent's window.
sheets.lifecycle: Evaluated at startup for each of the four locked surfaces on every launch on that machine: user-level and project-level sources are skipped while plugin and managed sources still load. It stops applying only when IT changes the managed policy.
sheets.failure_mode: Fails closed for the four named surfaces, but its scope is exactly those four. CLAUDE.md, .claude/rules, slash commands and output styles are not locked by it, so repo-supplied instructions still reach the model. Without disableSideloadFlags a developer can also bypass the marketplace pin for a single run with --plugin-dir, --plugin-url, --agents or --mcp-config.
sheets.version_caveat: disableSideloadFlags requires Claude Code v2.1.193 or later, so an un-upgraded laptop keeps the CLI bypass. Both keys are managed-settings-only and have no effect in user or project files. Unrecognised surface names in the array are ignored rather than rejected, so an older client silently enforces less than the policy states.

sheets.primary: Managed settings carrying strictPluginOnlyCustomization set to true, so hooks, skills, agents and MCP servers load only from plugins or from managed settings, combined with strictKnownMarketplaces plus a force-enabled enabledPlugins list to control which plugins exist and disableSideloadFlags to close the CLI bypass. That quartet covers exactly the four surfaces named: automation scripts are hooks, on-demand instruction packages are skills, custom agent definitions are agents, and external tool servers are MCP.
sheets.rejected_alternative: allowManagedHooksOnly on its own, which is the nearest single key but locks only the hooks surface; skills, agent definitions and .mcp.json servers from a developer's home directory or a repo would still load.
sheets.enforcement_owner: The harness. Claude Code decides at load time which sources it will read, and the setting is honoured only from managed settings, so no user or project file can re-open a locked surface.
sheets.context_boundary: This is a startup-time loading decision outside every context window: for each locked surface Claude Code skips user-level and project-level directories entirely, so a rogue skill or agent never reaches a session and never consumes context.
sheets.lifecycle: It applies from process start for every session on the machine while the managed payload is present, per surface, and stops applying if IT removes the key or narrows the array. Plugin-provided and managed-directory components continue to load throughout.
sheets.failure_mode: Fails closed for the four surfaces, but the guarantee is only as good as the supply chain around it: unrecognised surface names in the array are ignored rather than rejected, so a typo silently leaves that surface open, and without the marketplace allowlist a developer can still install some other plugin whose components would then load legitimately.
sheets.version_caveat: disableSideloadFlags, which rejects --plugin-dir, --plugin-url, --agents and --mcp-config at startup, requires Claude Code v2.1.193 or later; on earlier builds a developer can bypass the marketplace allowlist for a single run with those flags. strictPluginOnlyCustomization and allowManagedHooksOnly are managed-settings-only keys and have no effect anywhere else.

sheets.primary: strictPluginOnlyCustomization set to true in managed settings, which locks exactly the four surfaces named (hooks, skills, agents, mcp) to plugin-provided or managed sources, combined with strictKnownMarketplaces to pin the marketplace, extraKnownMarketplaces to pre-register it, and enabledPlugins in managed settings to force-enable the IT plugins.
sheets.rejected_alternative: Shipping the same components as a plugin and asking everyone to install it, without the managed lock. Plugin distribution is purely additive: a developer's ~/.claude/skills/, a repo's .claude/agents/, project settings hooks and a project .mcp.json would all still load beside the sanctioned plugin.
sheets.enforcement_owner: The harness. Claude Code decides which sources it discovers and loads at startup; managed settings are the top precedence tier and cannot be overridden.
sheets.context_boundary: Discovery and loading happen in the CLI process before the session exists, so a blocked skill, agent, hook or MCP server never enters the model's context at all: its instructions and tools are absent rather than present-and-refused. Only the plugin-provided and managed components contribute anything to the context window.
sheets.lifecycle: Evaluated when Claude Code loads configuration at session start and on configuration refresh, and it governs the whole session; the marketplace restriction is additionally enforced on marketplace add and on plugin install, update, refresh and auto-update. It stops applying only when the device stops receiving the managed policy.
sheets.failure_mode: Fails closed for the four locked surfaces, but coverage is exactly those four: slash commands, output styles, CLAUDE.md and .claude/rules/ are not locked by this key, so repo-committed instruction text still reaches the model. Add allowManagedHooksOnly and allowManagedMcpServersOnly as reinforcement, and expect support load when developers' existing personal skills and agents silently stop loading with no per-item explanation.
sheets.version_caveat: strictPluginOnlyCustomization is readable only from managed settings and takes either true or an array such as ["skills", "hooks"]; unrecognized surface names are ignored rather than failing the file, so newer names are safe to add early. Close the per-run bypass with disableSideloadFlags, which rejects --plugin-dir, --plugin-url, --agents and --mcp-config at startup and requires Claude Code v2.1.193 or later.

sheets.primary: An enterprise managed-settings policy file deployed by MDM at the system path and owned by an administrator, which both ships the approved extensions (ideally as a single IT-controlled plugin from an IT-controlled marketplace, bundling the hooks, skills, subagents and MCP server definitions) and disables discovery of the user-level and project-level equivalents, including the flags that would otherwise let a repo's own MCP server definitions be enabled.
sheets.rejected_alternative: Distributing a blessed .claude directory into every repo as the source of truth, rejected because project-level configuration is exactly what a developer can edit or add to, so it cannot be the thing that decides what is allowed to load.
sheets.enforcement_owner: The harness at the top settings precedence tier, backed by OS file ownership so the policy itself cannot be edited locally. The model has no say in which extensions exist.
sheets.context_boundary: The policy is evaluated at session startup, outside any context window. What the model sees is simply a narrower menu: the approved skills, subagents and tools appear and nothing else does.
sheets.lifecycle: Read at the start of every session on a managed machine and re-applied by MDM on drift. It stops governing anything launched from an unmanaged install, a container image the developer built, or the Agent SDK used directly.
sheets.failure_mode: Fails closed for the extension surfaces the policy actually enumerates, and fails open for any surface it does not. That is the durable weakness: each new extension type added to the product defaults to loading until the policy is updated, so this control needs review at every upgrade. It also does not stop behavioural influence, since repo files and CLAUDE.md text still steer the agent even when no developer-authored code loads.
sheets.version_caveat: I am confident managed settings exist and can constrain MCP server loading (including a project-MCP enable flag and a disallowed-servers list), but I cannot verify from model knowledge alone that current managed settings expose keys to suppress user-level and project-level hooks, skills and subagent definitions, nor the plugin-marketplace pinning keys or their plan gating. The full guarantee as stated should be treated as unproven until the available managed keys are enumerated against the installed version.
